To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the throughput of a receiver depends on its smoothness of in order packet delivery, (ii) the smoothness of one user can be used to increase the throughput of another, and (iii) the smoothness and throughput of both users can be increased simultaneously.

the throughput-smoothness curve for a multicast stream to two users has a concave shape with a minimum throughput at an in-order packet delivery smoothness value that depends on the channel erasure probabilities, and that the throughput-smoothing curve is a lower bound on the throughput-smooth curve for a stream multicast to any number of users.

(a) The trade-off between throughput and smoothness of in order packet delivery is characterized by a Markov chain with a state space that is the Cartesian product of the state spaces of the two users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How does a source trade-off throughput for in-order delivery?
the following question: how can the source use feedback to maximize the number of in-order packets delivered at each of the users?
the design of multicast coding schemes that can adapt to different trade-offs of throughput-smoothness for different applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for the case of two users, the optimal throughput-smoothness region is characterized by the union of the convex hulls of the regions corresponding to the two users, and that this characterization is tight.

the throughput-smoothness performance of a multicast scheme depends on the channel erasure probabilities and the number of users, and that a coding scheme can achieve the maximum throughput-smoothness point on each trade-off curve.
for the case of two users and independent channels, the optimal trade-off is achieved by the scheme proposed in this paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a general framework for analyzing throughput and smoothness trade-offs of two users in multicasting of ordered streams, and propose coding and scheduling schemes that can span these trade-offs.
the throughput of in-order delivery can be as high as 0.5, 0.75, 0.875, and 1 for 2, 3, 4 and 5 users, respectively.
we show how the throughput and in-order packet delivery can be traded-off for the users in the presence of feedback.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the throughput-smoothness performance of the users is interdependent.
the throughput-smoothness performance of an ordered stream is fundamentally different from that of a random stream.
, in contrast to previous results, the throughput-smoothness performance of the users need not be the same, and that the smoothness can be traded off with throughput.
